datasets.title: Faroe Islands: Copernicus Vegetation Index Anomaly (FAPAR Anomaly)
datasets.description: Fraction of Absorbed Photosynthetically Active Radiation (FAPAR) is a biophysical dimensionless quantity (its values range from 0/no absorption to 1/total absorption) used to assess the greenness and health of vegetation. FAPAR anomalies can be used as an indicator to detect and monitor the impacts of agricultural drought on the growth and productivity of vegetation. The data is presented in 10-day time composite of the Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS).. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/fro-anomalies-fapar-viirs]
datasets.details: Variations in the vegetation health and/or cover could be related to stress factors not related to droughts (e.g., plant diseases, pests, hail, flooding). To determine if changes in FAPAR are linked with a drought event or not, FAPAR data should be interpreted jointly with other indicators (as in the EDO Combined Drought Indicator).

entity.name: Copernicus / European Commission Joint Research Centre (JRC)

lineage.description: FAPAR values derived from VIIRS satellite radiometer observations are composited at 10-day intervals. Anomalies are calculated at each grid cell as the deviation from a long-term mean baseline (2012 to last complete year), producing raster datasets that serve as an empirical indicator of agricultural drought stress on vegetation productivity.

sources.name: Copernicus / European Commission Joint Research Centre (JRC)
sources.description: VIIRS satellite-derived FAPAR observations processed into 10-day composites with anomaly calculations relative to 2012-present baseline to provide continuous monitoring of vegetation stress indicators for drought detection
